newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile close to deal for French-Spanish submarines.
newsitem.headline: Chile close to deal for French-Spanish submarines.

text.p: Chile is close to a deal to buy two modern submarines built by a Franco-Spanish consortium for about $500 million but has not yet ruled out a competing German design, Defence Minister Edmundo Perez Yoma said on Tuesday.

The Scorpene-type submarines, sold by the DCNI-Bazan consortium, would replace the navy's ageing British-built submarines as part of what defence officials call an overall modernisation of Chile's arsenal.

"The Chilean government is indeed going to buy some submarines. We are leaning strongly toward the French-Spanish submarines and we are in final negotiations for them," Perez Yoma told a news conference.

But he said a German submarine had not been ruled out despite media reports the German government had vetoed the sale until Chile's former dictator Gen. Augusto Pinochet, 82, leaves his post as army commander-in-chief in March 1998.

"The submarine most in line with what the navy is looking for is the French-Spanish one so we're wrapping up details to bring the negotiations to a happy conclusion. We hope to have a final decision in the middle of June," Perez Yoma said.

Chile bought 67 German-built battle tanks from Belgium and plans to buy up to 200 hundred more over the next couple of years as part of a campaign to replace ageing weaponry with newer, mostly European hardware.

U.S. arms dealers have been unable to bid in the deals because of Washington's virtual ban on weapons sales to the country since 1977, when Pinochet was in power. The Clinton administration has indicated recently it will relax the ban.
